WINNERS AND LOSERS
Winner: The Fightin' MacKinnon
According to HockeyFights.com, Colorado Avalanche star Nathan MacKinnon has had three fights in the NHL. His first was in Dec. 2024. His next two have come in a two week span this season.

Mac dropped the gloves against Brandt Clarke of the Los Angeles Kings on Sept. 30 and then had a spirited bout with Roope Hintz during the Frozen Frenzy, coming up bloody against the Dallas center.

"The way we all grow up in the Maritimes, it's pretty gritty. Most guys from that area are pretty feisty," he said. "I might be done for the year, but you never know."

Loser: Injuries
MacKinnon escaped his fight with some stitches and welts, which is welcome news, considering how the rest of the NHL seems to be its own hospital wing these days.

Igor Shesterkin is done for the year with a knee injury. The Panthers are without Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov. Rasmus Dahlin is out. Brock Faber and Nico Sturm suffered horrific puck to the head injuries.

The Hurricanes lost Jordan Staal for at least a month and then saw Taylor Hall injured. Matt Duchene is out three months. Mathew Barzal remains sidelined, as are Jake Sanderson and Travis Konecny.

It's never good when the guys on the injury report could create a better starting lineup than 90% of the league.

Winner: Committing to the Wheel
When I spoke with Alex DeBrincat last month, he wasn't sure if he'd remain a Red Wing for the entirety of the season. His contract was up, and he was looking at a hefty raise. But even as his now-former captain wanted out, the 28-year-old winger wanted to re-sign.

"I love playing for the Red Wings. My intention is obviously to stay in Detroit. We'll see what happens, I guess," he said.

Here's what happened: DeBrincat signed a max term (seven years) deal worth $13 million annually. DeBrincat gets paid. Interim GM Shawn Horcoff gets a big win. And Red Wings fans can celebrate someone choosing to stay with the club at a time when others are trying escape.

Loser: PWHL Vegas Jerseys
The PWHL released the jersey designs for their four new expansion teams:

Detroit's is fire. Hamilton's is pretty striking. San Jose's is giving "unlicensed NHL video game" but they're ultimately fine.

But Vegas ... sweet Vegas. What are we doing? The P-Dub said the inspiration for this design was "inspired by the natural scenery of Southern Nevada," including navy stripes that "nod to the desert at night."

I can't stress this enough: You're. In. Las. Vegas. A city of glamour and neon lights. A place whose iconography is conjured the minute someone says "Vegas." Where's the gaudiness? The glitz? I wanted aura and you gave me algae.

Winner: Brady Tkachuk
We had him as a loser last week, so it's only fair we give him the W for an absolutely dominant Frozen Frenzy performance: a natural hat trick in the second period of a 7-3 win against the Columbus Blue Jackets. It was the first natural hatty in NHL history in which the goal-scorer's sibling assisted on all three goals, as Matthew did for Brady.

In a wild stat, Brady is the ninth player in NHL history to have his brother assist on all three goals of a hat trick. The player for whom that happened the most: Daniel Sedin, who had Henrik assist on his hatty three times.

Loser: Defense

Tuesday night ended with 112 goals scored, three more than the previous record high in the Frozen Frenzy. (Thanks, Bruins' 6-3 win at San Jose!) It just missed setting a record for the most goals scored in a single day in NHL history, eclipsed only by the 114 goals scored on Nov. 4, 2023, which had 30 teams in action and the Penguins hanging 10 on the Sharks.

Through 105 games, the NHL was averaging 3.10 goals per game and a league-wide save percentage of .891, which would be the lowest since 1992-93 if it held. Last season was the first with a sub-.900 league save percentage in 20 years. The lamps are being lit.

FAVORITE OFF-ICE MOMENT
As a massive fan of competition cooking shows and the bromance between Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith, the San Jose Sharks' Elevated Cupcake Experience might be the greatest thing to emerge from the baking world since sprinkles.

In a stunt that benefitted the Sharks Foundation, Team Celebrini and Team Smith battled in the Frost Cupcake Factory kitchen to develop the M.E.C. -- the Most Elevated Cupcake. The cupcakes were blind judged by broadcaster Brodie Brazil, Sharks winger Tyler Toffoli and podcaster Cat Toffoli.

We don't want to give away the winner, but we will say that the one great cupcake outweighed the several good cupcakes made by the losing team. And in the end, the Elevated Cupcake Cup was raised to the sky.

MUST-SEE GAMES

Utah Mammoth at Edmonton Oilers

Thursday, Oct. 15, 9 p.m. ET

The Mammoth are 5-2-0 to start the season, looking like they're ready to level up from playoff neophyte to title contender in the West. The Oilers are 5-0-1 and have eschewed their firewagon hockey nature for a bit more structure -- they're down around eight shot attempts per 60 minutes at 5-on-5 year over year. Really looking forward to this as a test for both teams, and they'll run it back in Salt Lake City on Saturday night.

Pittsburgh Penguins at Colorado Avalanche

Friday, Oct. 16, 9 p.m. ET

Look, I hate thinking this way. Blame Alex Ovechkin. But we're creeping forever closer to not having Battle of Cole Harbour games between Sidney Crosby and Nathan MacKinnon anymore, as the Penguins captain plays in his 22nd NHL season. Relish it. Cherish it. Hey, maybe they'll even have a fight for us.

FROM YOUR HOCKEY FRIENDS AT ESPN

Roger McQueen kept the Pixar "Cars" references coming during his NHL debut.
Last week's NHL power rankings. This St. Louis Blues disrespect will not stand.
One the latest edition of The Drop, Emily Kaplan and I dropped takes on the biggest news items in the NHL, Connor Hellebuyck's future to whether the league is headed to Texas with expansion.

PUCK HEADLINES
DATELINE: Philadelphia
It's said that life comes at you fast. Well, there's fast and then there's Philadelphia sports fast. In May, Rick Tocchet was coaching the Flyers in the second round of the playoffs, snapping a six-season playoff drought and eliminating the rival Penguins in the opening round. On October, fans were chanting for him to lose his job as the Flyers failed to win a game in their first eight tries.

You know it's bad when fans are creating websites to encourage the dismissal of a coach. Fire The Taco went online this week -- the name is a reference to Trevor Zegras' nickname for Tocchet -- complete with a fan petition to sign and the ability to throw digital tacos at the Flyers bench, because "real tacos on the ice will get you escorted out by Gritty personally."

Daniel, a die-hard Flyers fan, created the site. "The writing was on the wall that the fan base -- especially toxic Hockey Twitter - was going to start the Fire Tocchet talk. So I wanted to get ahead of it and create a space for all of us to voice our displeasure," he told ESPN.

For what it's worth, the NHL sources I've spoken to believe there's zero chance that Tocchet gets fired for this atrocious start, with the blame falling squarely on the players, their preparation and execution. He's also in Year 2 of a five-year contract that reportedly pays him over $5 million a season. Comcast Spectacor would probably prefer not to pay a guy $15 million to not coach.

DATELINE: Las Vegas
One of the biggest stories in the NHL in the past week was the end of the Vegas Golden Knights' run of sellouts, which was broken last Thursday in a shootout win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Sin Bin had an interesting story looking into the potential causes for the nine-season sellout streak to end, with reasons ranging from the relationship between the team and its fans to the decline of Canadian tourism in Las Vegas, which was down over 17% last year.

Sin Bin notes one interesting change in policy that might have impacted attendance: "The Golden Knights cut out ticket brokers during last year's playoffs, prioritizing additional revenue over relationships with partners they had worked with for a decade."

The Golden Knights aren't the first NHL team to wrestle back tickets from brokers. The Rangers did that years ago, too. It's my understanding that the team's season-ticket renewal rate was a concern: Vegas was renewing between 60-70% in some years, with a target of 90%. The ticket broker issue was an inflection point: Season-ticket holders couldn't sell their own inventory because the brokers were undercutting them by flooding the market with available seats.

Again, there's an imperfect storm of reasons why attendance is suddenly a topic of conversation for a team that played for the Stanley Cup last season. In fact one of them mentioned by Sin Bin is "success fatigue." (That sound you heard was 30 other fan bases doing a spit-take.)

DATELINE: Jack Hughes
The Devils have three wins on the season. Jack Hughes owns two of them with a pair of overtime goals, giving him 11 goals in the 3-on-3 during his NHL career.

Watching Hughes and linemate Jesper Bratt operate in overtime basically justifies the format: Two offensive wizards exhibiting Sedins-like chemistry on open ice. The Devils know the advantage they have in the 3-on-3 with those two on the roster. This preseason, coach Sheldon Keefe decided to lean into it. He moved up overtime and shootout drills much earlier in training camp than usual -- not because camp was truncated but because "it had been an afterthought in the past," he said.

"It's part of the identity of our group. If we can get [to overtime], we're in a really good spot to get that second point," he said. "Generally speaking, overtime is a coin toss. A lot of stuff can happen and go wrong. But we certainly like the players that we have to be able on the right side of it more often than not."

Especially when one of those players is Jack Hughes. Just ask Team Canada.

stories.headline: Man United 'a circus' amid Lisandro Martínez rant - Roy Keane
stories.summary: Roy Keane has branded Manchester United a "circus" following Lisandro Martínez's outburst against the club's hierarchy.
stories.body:
Roy Keane has branded Manchester United a "circus" following Lisandro Martínez's outburst against the club's hierarchy.

Argentina defender Martínez accused the club of lacking ambition and questioned their summer recruitment after Tuesday night's 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atlético Madrid.

Former United defender Gary Neville said Martínez's comments amounted to a direct attack on his team-mates and suggested senior players would be "absolutely fuming," while ex-captain Keane described the remarks as symptomatic of the "chaos" at Old Trafford.

"They're obviously not together," Keane said of the club, speaking on The Overlap's Stick to Football podcast. "It is chaotic there from the top to the bottom. We go there on match days and I don't like the feeling around the club.

"It just seems chaotic -- statements can reflect it. It was chaotic with how they got to (Michael] Carrick as their manager.

"We said from day one there were better options out there, and maybe the players are looking at there's better options as players out there. It's chaos, it's like a circus."

Lisandro Martínez rant riles Man United legends

Martínez hit out at director of football Jason Wilcox and the United board in a caustic interview amid the club's worst start to a league season since 1986.

Neville and Keane shared some of Martínez's concerns about the state of the club.

However, both questioned the World Cup winner's individual performances and whether he had sufficient standing to make such comments.

"When Martínez says they should have brought more players in, he's directly attacking his team-mates," said Neville.

"If I was Bruno Fernandes and I was Harry Maguire and the other senior players, I'd be absolutely fuming with him because you're basically saying that some of us shouldn't be here and we should be bringing more players in.

"That's what I think he's saying."

Martínez attempted to take the sting out of the situation in a statement issued on Instagram on Wednesday.

"I don't think it will be a big falling out," said Keane. "Because I think we've question marks over this dressing room anyway.

"I don't think there's enough characters, enough men in there. We know that.

"But I don't see him as a senior player at Man United; I see him as a centre-half who's making lots of mistakes."

- Martínez exposes Man United's harsh reality: Blame lies with top brass, not Carrick

- Transfer rumors, news: Martínez's future at Man United in doubt after bust-up

- Wayne Rooney criticises Cristiano Ronaldo over Portugal walkout: 'Wrong in every sense'

United have not publicly responded to the remarks but were assessing their defender's comments before deciding whether to take disciplinary action, sources told ESPN.

"I thought it was really strange to have a go at Jason Wilcox, not because he's above criticism but the budget is not going to be set by Jason Wilcox; the budget is going to be set by the owners," said Neville.

"It was obvious they needed more defenders. He [Martínez] would probably be one of the first on the chopping block if players were actually brought in."

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Ferreira, De Sousa Brito help Dallas end Sounders' unbeaten run with 1-0 victory
stories.summary: Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half to give FC Dallas a 1-0 victory over Seattle Sounders on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half and Daniel De Sousa Britto made it stand up as FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0 on Wednesday night, ending the Sounders' four-match win streak and an unbeaten run that reached nine.

Ferreira took a pass from defender Osaze Urhoghide in the 63rd minute and scored for the fourth time this season after scoring twice in 27 appearances as a 19-year-old rookie last year. Urhoghide's helper was his third after collecting one last season in 27 matches as a rookie.

De Sousa Britto finished with seven saves for his third clean sheet in six starts with Dallas (14-7-8). He had 14 shutouts in 78 career starts with the San Jose Earthquakes before joining the club.

Andrew Thomas totaled two saves for Seattle (11-10-8), which went 4-0-5 during its unbeaten streak.

Seattle beat Dallas 2-1 at home to close out April.

Dallas improves to 7-2-5 at home, while the Sounders drop to 4-6-5 on the road.

Up next Seattle: Hosts CF Montreal on Saturday.

Dallas: At Houston Dynamo on Saturday.

stories.headline: 'I'm a competitor': Cody Walker primed and ready for the next step
stories.summary: Cody Walker has lived a year of Carlton's ups and downs before having even been drafted. He's learned a lot about the business of footy and what he needs to do to take the next step, as his own AFL career begins.
stories.body:
Cody Walker had a front row seat to Carlton's tumultuous season. In line meetings, at team dinners, out of the Michael Voss era and into the Josh Fraser fairytale. From door stops to crisis meetings, it was an eye opening introduction to the big business of footy for the son-of-a-gun.

"I actually reflect on it a bit now and consider how low a club can get. Being on the inside with all the outside noise that we had when all the Vossy stuff was going down, it was really quite interesting to see," Walker tells ESPN.

"Then going from that to top of the AFL and beating Brisbane and Fremantle towards the end of the season, seeing how good a club can feel and get. For that to both happen in one season I find it quite interesting. I'm sort of glad it happened in a way that I get to experience both worlds."

In the midst of their early season malaise, Blues players were subjected to abuse walking off the ground after second half fadeouts and even rocked up to Ikon Park with anti-Voss graffiti on the club walls. That included Walker as he trained full-time with the squad.

"All the outside noise tears you apart a little bit. To see fans out the front of Ikon Park sort of giving it to you, and open training to have people yelling out at you and it's your fans, they've got Carlton stuff on, but they're yelling out to you, it's pretty full on."

From 1-8 under Voss, the Blues stormed home under Fraser, winning their next six starts and claiming a remarkable win in a wildcard final against Melbourne.

A fractured playing group was united under a first-time head coach and Walker was along for the ride.

"It was quite an eye opener how sad it can get inside a club. You sort of have to keep to yourself in those moments and just get around the boys," he says.

"We definitely had to stick together as a group, and Fraser's been really good at that. We did a lot together this year, the players grabbed me along to every dinner they had. It was so good, such a good experience."

That finals finish means Carlton receives no discount on matching a bid on the son of high-flyer Andrew, with the pair likely to become the first father-son duo to each be selected in the top five of an AFL Draft.

Walker's talent deserves to see him taken at pick 2, just like his dad.

An electric midfielder blessed with the twitchiness, agility and burst to free himself from stoppages, Walker enjoyed a brilliant campaign with Carlton's VFL side and cemented his status in the 2026 draft.

There's no doubting his mercurial talent and its fit alongside Patrick Cripps, Sam Walsh, and Jagga Smith, but Walker isn't yet the complete package, and he's the first one to acknowledge it.

"I think my burst out of stoppage and ball-winning is my 'one wood'... when I look back on footage and see for myself how dangerous I can look going out of stoppage, it's really eye-opening for me," he tells ESPN.

"My improvements I want going into next year, I want to improve every part of my fundamentals. I've got a little bit of disposal efficiency which can let me down, but I'll put a power of work into kicking and handballing.

"It got to the point where I was doing two or three sessions a week, and that includes Diesel Williams helping me out.

"I've got so many good people around me and I can already feel that I'm getting better at those things. I'm pretty straightforward in what I want to get better at and I like getting harsh feedback from coaches that I can work on.

"No one's really pissing in my pocket about something I need to work on and I don't realise it until I'm maybe on [the MCG] one day and it's a problem for me if I'm missing kicks or missing handballs."

Walker's final game before he turns professional wasn't in Carlton's VFL side, at the national championships with Vic Country or back with the Bendigo Pioneers. It was in the Goulburn Valley Football League playing for hometown Echuca, and he spent most of his lead-up convincing the Blues' General Manager of Football to let him go.

"I actually sat down with Chris Davies about two weeks before the granny. I was like, 'What are the chances I get to play?'" Walker recalls to ESPN.

"He was like, 'Mate, we're not going to stop you. Preferably, I think it's the wrong decision, but it's all your choice.'"

Walker was determined to enjoy one more stint out in the country with his best mates after a massive top-age season, but injured his ankle during training the week after that conversation with Davies. It ruled him out of the qualifying final, but he still had an eye towards their qualification into the big dance.

"I went home for two weeks and I was training with Echuca and I just got addicted. I called up the club and a few people there and I was like 'I think I'm going to play, I'm doing it'. I'm so glad I did it."

Walker had 20 disposals, eight score involvements, and kicked a goal off the wing in Echuca's 13-goal win over the Shepparton Swans.

It underlined the values that have made Walker rise and rise through junior football ranks. His competitive spirit and genuine love of footy through rich bloodlines continually stands out. Carlton supporters have known of Walker's footballing exploits for years, but they may not know what makes him tick.

That attitude was on show in the 2km time trial at the AFL Draft combine. Walker led his group of runners by the length of the straight, finishing nine seconds ahead of second place. It's his inner motivation that drives him to compete against the best, and oftentimes that means competing against himself.

It's why he has a grin on his face when asked why he even ran despite some Blues supporters bemoaning his name rising higher on rival clubs' draft boards.

"It was probably to beat my [personal best]... my PB was 6:13, I was feeling good and I had a bit in the tank," he says.

"Personally I'm a competitor. I do want to see where I'm at as of right now compared to maybe three months later when I do a 2k at the club."

Walker smashed that time, finishing in 6:04 minutes and on the podium despite running in a slower pack.

It's given Carlton more to consider, lacking the points to match a bid at pick 1 but desperate to secure its second elite father-son prospect in as many years after Harry Dean was taken with pick two in 2025.

"I've got plenty of trust in the club with what they can do in my scenario," Walker says.

"I love the Carlton Football Club and I'm really thankful they've given me this year and it would be a really cool thing to end up at my dad's club. There's a lot of history there."

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."
